**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve multiline attributes when cutting declarations**

When an item has a multiline attribute such as `#[derive(\nClone,\n)]`, the line immediately above the declaration is `)]`, so this backward scan stops and leaves the entire attribute in the source. If another item follows, the attribute silently attaches to that item while the moved declaration loses it; both files can still type-check, so `apply` can change `cfg`, derives, or other semantics without reporting a problem. Determine the complete outer-attribute span rather than recognizing only lines beginning with `#[`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Convert LSP UTF-16 columns before rewriting references**

LSP columns default to UTF-16 code units, but this converts `col` by counting Rust `char`s. When a reference appears after a supplementary character such as an emoji on the same line, the computed offset lands after the symbol, `requalify` skips it, and a bare reference may receive no import after the move. In the source file this can be applied despite leaving an unresolved call because the diagnostics fallback deliberately does not flag missing symbols in the file they were removed from.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

findings.conclusion: Move references now use strict shared UTF-16-to-byte conversion. Supplementary characters no longer shift offsets by counting Rust chars, and unmatched references block even forced writes.

current_evidence.observation: Item-move offset_of delegates to the shared converter.
Strict 1-based conversion walks LF/CRLF and rejects invalid/surrogate-interior columns.
Supplementary characters count as two units.
Parsing changes coordinate origin without altering the UTF-16 character count.
The actual reference rewrite uses the corrected converter.
Pre-rewrite matching uses the same converter.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject target files outside the crate module tree**

The target is only checked for existence and then assigned a module path from its filesystem location; there is no verification that its parent actually declares it. Moving an unreferenced public item to an existing orphan such as `src/home.rs` without `mod home;` can therefore produce no error diagnostics and be applied, while the item disappears from the compiled crate and breaks downstream users. Verify the target is present in rust-analyzer's module tree before constructing or applying the move.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retain nested paths when narrowing grouped imports**

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read visibility from the declaration rather than the item prefix**

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Choose the crate root that owns the moved item**

In a package containing both `src/lib.rs` and `src/main.rs`, moving an item from the binary into a new `src/util.rs` always declares the module in `lib.rs`. The later module-path logic still treats `main.rs` as the same crate and rewrites its references as `crate::util::...`, but that module is absent from the binary crate root, so validation rejects an otherwise valid move. The source's owning root must disambiguate which parent receives the declaration.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict `super::` rewriting to paths in the module scope**

When the moved source contains `super::` in a string literal, comment, macro token, or nested inline module, this byte scan rewrites it as well. For example, `const HELP: &str = "super::help";` silently changes runtime data while still type-checking, and `mod inner { super::f(); }` is incorrectly redirected from the moved module to its old parent. Tokenize the source and rewrite only path expressions whose `super` actually resolves to the original parent.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not recurse through symlinked module directories**

If the module's submodule directory contains a symlink to a directory, `Path::is_dir` follows it and this recursion treats every target file as part of the module. Applying the move then copies those files and deletes their old paths through the symlink, potentially deleting files outside the checkout; a cyclic directory symlink can also recurse indefinitely. Inspect `symlink_metadata` and reject or preserve directory symlinks rather than traversing them.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update every crate root that declares a top-level module**

When a package has both `src/lib.rs` and `src/main.rs`, a top-level file such as `src/a.rs` may be declared by either or both roots, but `declaring_file` delegates to `parent_module_file`, which always selects the existing `lib.rs` first. If only the binary declares the module the move is incorrectly refused; if both roots declare it, the move updates only the library declaration and deletes the shared file, leaving the unchanged binary with a missing module that the edited-file-only analyzer check need not report.
